citations.authors: Bartels EM, Juhl CB, Christensen R, et al.
citations.title: Aquatic exercise for the treatment of knee and hip osteoarthritis
citations.what_it_says: Cochrane review of 13 RCTs (n=1190): aquatic exercise produces small but clinically relevant short-term improvements in pain, disability, and QoL in knee/hip OA.

citations.authors: Bidonde J, Busch AJ, Webber SC, et al.
citations.title: Aquatic exercise training for fibromyalgia
citations.what_it_says: Cochrane review of 16 trials (n=881): aquatic training improves wellness, symptoms, fitness, and pain in fibromyalgia, with effects comparable to land-based exercise.

citations.authors: Waller B, Ogonowska-Slodownik A, Vitor M, et al.
citations.title: Effect of therapeutic aquatic exercise on symptoms and function associated with lower limb osteoarthritis: systematic review with meta-analysis
citations.what_it_says: Meta-analysis of 11 studies (n=1092): aquatic exercise significantly reduces pain and stiffness and improves function in lower-limb OA.

citations.authors: Batterham SI, Heywood S, Keating JL
citations.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis comparing land and aquatic exercise for people with hip or knee arthritis on function, mobility and other health outcomes
citations.what_it_says: Head-to-head meta-analysis: aquatic and land-based exercise produce comparable outcomes in hip/knee arthritis — water is an equivalent option for those who cannot tolerate land exercise.

citations.authors: Mehrholz J, Kugler J, Pohl M
citations.title: Water-based exercises for improving activities of daily living after stroke
citations.what_it_says: Cochrane review: limited evidence suggests water-based exercise after stroke may benefit ADLs and strength, though trials were few and small.

citations.authors: Iliescu AM, McIntyre A, Wiener J, et al.
citations.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of aquatic therapy on mobility, balance, and level of functional independence in stroke rehabilitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
citations.what_it_says: Meta-analysis in stroke: aquatic therapy produced significant improvements in mobility and balance versus land-based therapy.

citations.authors: Cugusi L, Manca A, Bergamin M, et al.
citations.title: Aquatic exercise improves motor impairments in people with Parkinson's disease, with similar or greater benefits than land-based exercise: a systematic review
citations.what_it_says: Systematic review in PD: aquatic exercise improves motor impairments, balance, and fear of falling, with benefits similar to or greater than land-based exercise.

citations.authors: Gomes Neto M, Pontes SS, Almeida LO, et al.
citations.title: Effects of water-based exercise on functioning and quality of life in people with Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
citations.what_it_says: Meta-analysis: water-based exercise improves balance, mobility, and quality of life in Parkinson's disease.

citations.authors: Amedoro A, Berardi A, Conte A, et al.
citations.title: The effect of aquatic physical therapy on patients with multiple sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis
citations.what_it_says: Meta-analysis in MS: aquatic PT benefits fatigue, balance, and function; recommended as an integration with conventional therapy.

citations.authors: Roostaei M, Baharlouei H, Azadi H, Fragala-Pinkham MA
citations.title: Effects of Aquatic Intervention on Gross Motor Skills in Children with Cerebral Palsy: A Systematic Review
citations.what_it_says: Systematic review of 11 studies in pediatric CP: aquatic intervention shows promising gross-motor improvements with good feasibility and enjoyment.

citations.authors: Shi Z, Zhou H, Lu L, et al.
citations.title: Aquatic Exercises in the Treatment of Low Back Pain: A Systematic Review of the Literature and Meta-Analysis of Eight Studies
citations.journal: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
citations.what_it_says: Meta-analysis of 8 RCTs: aquatic exercise significantly reduces pain and disability in low back pain versus control interventions.

citations.authors: Peng MS, Wang R, Wang YZ, et al.
citations.title: Efficacy of Therapeutic Aquatic Exercise vs Physical Therapy Modalities for Patients With Chronic Low Back Pain: A Randomized Clinical Trial
citations.what_it_says: RCT (n=113, 12-month follow-up): aquatic exercise produced greater improvements in disability, pain, QoL, sleep, and mental state than PT modalities for chronic low back pain.

citations.authors: Waller B, Ogonowska-Slodownik A, Vitor M, et al.
citations.title: The effect of aquatic exercise on physical functioning in the older adult: a systematic review with meta-analysis
citations.what_it_says: Meta-analysis in older adults: aquatic exercise improves physical functioning, comparable to land-based exercise and superior to no intervention.
